# ComfyUI Params Inspector
**One PNG is a full recipe.** Drop a ComfyUI image on the page and you get the workflow that produce
d it, the whole LoRA chain, and every sampler setting — export it as-is, or pour those parameters in
to your own template and get a fresh workflow back.
A single page you open by double-clicking `index.html`. No dependencies, no uploads: images never le
ave your machine and nothing touches the network.
> Every filename, model name, LoRA name and prompt in the screenshot is synthetic demo data, unrelat
ed to any real asset. The UI itself is in Simplified Chinese.
## What it does, in thirty seconds
| What you want | What you get |
| "How was this image made?" | Drop the PNG (or a whole `output` folder) → LoRA order and strengths,

seed / steps / CFG / sampler, base model, CLIP, VAE, both prompts |
| "I want to reproduce that res
ult" | Click **export this image's workflow JSON** → a `.workflow.json` you can drop back onto a Com

fyUI canvas |
| "The PNG has parameters but no canvas graph" | Load a template workflow → **rebuild
from template** → every parameter (including the full LoRA chain) is poured in and a new workflow is

written out |
| "I need the parameters for a few hundred old images" | Export CSV / JSON, or batch-
pack every workflow into a zip |
## Four things you think you can see, but can't
1. **On the canvas ≠ in the run.** The demo image has `#91` and `#92` sitting right there — both `mo
de: 4` (bypassed), absent from the execution graph entirely. They get their own list here: *present

but not part of the render*.
2. **Reading the prompt directly gives you an empty string.** `CLIPText
Encode.text` is usually blank because the text arrives over a **link** (the output of `ZhPromptEnhan
ce`, say). The tool walks the link to its source and names it: `CLIPTextEncode#4.text[slot 0] ← ZhPr

omptEnhance#79.text[slot 0]`.
3. **The negative prompt may be computed at runtime.** Slot 1 of an en
hancer is generated on the spot and never stored in the PNG. It is marked *generated at runtime* ins

tead of passing the enhancer's input off as the result.
4. **Parameters are scattered across dozens
of nodes.** Seventeen LoRAs chained together, each at its own strength — the tool climbs back from `
KSampler.model` and lists them in true execution order.
## Features
- **Browse**: pick a folder (recursive) / drop a folder / drop single PNGs. Inline thumbnails in the

list, a 212px preview that opens full-size in the detail pane.
- **Parameters**: seed, steps, CFG,
sampler / scheduler, denoise, latent, base model, CLIP (with type), VAE, save prefix, pre-sampler pa

tches (`ModelSamplingAuraFlow`, `CFGNorm`, …).
- **LoRA chain**: execution order plus strength, draw

n as a zero-centred slider (green positive, red negative), copyable as one line per LoRA.
- **Prompt

s**: link resolution with slot annotations, expandable and copyable.
- **Search**: filename / LoRA n

ame / prompt body. `Ctrl+K` to focus, `↑` `↓` to move.
- **Export**: parameter table as CSV (UTF-8 B

OM, opens cleanly in Excel) and as JSON.
- **Workflow export**: emit `.workflow.json` verbatim, or z

ip a whole batch.
- **Template rebuild**: use an existing workflow as a template, pour the parsed pa

rameters in, get a new workflow. The template is deep-cloned and never written back.
- **DeepSeek Ha
rness plugin**: the same parser ships as a DSH bundle exposing `comfy_png_inspect` to the model.
## Quick start
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Open **`comfy-png-inspector.html`** (Chrome / Edge 103+, `DecompressionStream` required) and drag yo
ur ComfyUI `output` folder into the window.
- The `index.html` at the repo root is a one-line redirect kept for GitHub Pages; opening it offline

lands on the app too.
- The UI is **bilingual (Chinese / English)**: switch with `中文 / EN` in the t

op bar, the choice is remembered, and the default follows your browser language.
- Force a language
with the URL: `comfy-png-inspector.html?lang=en` (or `?lang=zh`).
## Reproducing a workflow: two modes, don't mix them up
After selecting an image the detail pane offers two buttons. The difference is how much data the fil
cting an image the detail pane offers two buttons. The difference is how much data the file carries:
| | Export verbatim | Rebuild from template |

| Button | Export this image's workflow JSON | Rebuild from template |
| Needs | A `workflow` chunk

inside the PNG | Any canvas workflow loaded as a template |
| Result | The exact canvas from the mom
ent of generation — node positions, links, bypass state | The template's layout, with the parsed par

ameters poured in |
| Best for | Straight reproduction, most reliable | API-only PNGs, or mapping ba
ck onto the template you use today |
[该节后续省略]
## How it works
1. **PNG chunk parsing**: reads `tEXt` / `zTXt` / `iTXt`; `zTXt` and compressed `iTXt` are inflated

with `DecompressionStream('deflate')` (zlib stream).
2. **Chain tracing**: start at `KSampler.model`
and follow `inputs.model` backwards, bucketing by node class (`LoraLoader*` = slider, `CFGNorm` / `
ModelSampling*` = pre-sampler patch). Stops at `UNETLoader` / `CheckpointLoaderSimple`, then reverse

s into execution order.
3. **Bypass detection**: purely from `workflow.nodes[].mode` — `4` = bypass,
`2` = mute. These nodes are absent from the API graph, which is exactly why "on canvas" ≠ "in the r

un".
4. **Prompt resolution**: a string `text` is used as-is; a `[node_id, slot]` ref walks the link
to its source. Slot ≠ 0 means the value is produced at runtime, so it is not treated as a literal.
5. **Template rebuild**: deep-clone the template → strip its LoRA nodes and links → append new nodes
in parsed order and chain them → rewire the tail into the original consumer → self-check.
## Known limitations

- PNG only. ComfyUI metadata lives in PNG chunks; jpg / webp have none.
- Re-saving through a screen

shot tool, an IM app, or Photoshop drops the `tEXt` chunk — the UI will say "no ComfyUI metadata".
-
Under `file://` the browser will not let JavaScript scan a directory, so you must pick or drop once

per session.
- Rebuild is bounded by **the node classes present in the template**: a node class in
the PNG but not in the template will not be invented (LoRA nodes are the exception — recreated from

the parsed count). Read the change list before exporting.
- The zip writer is store-only (no compres
sion) to stay dependency-free; a few hundred workflows land in the low tens of MB.
